perf.summary: Row bases i*n and (i+1)*n are recomputed for all four array accesses every inner iteration; column index j+1 recomputed.
perf.currentCost: Per (i,j): two multiplies (i*n, (i+1)*n) folded into four index expressions plus repeated +j / +(j+1) address arithmetic, and four dependent loads feeding two adds and a compare.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist long* row0 = a + (long)i*n; long* row1 = a + (long)(i+1)*n; outside the j loop. Inner: `long lhs = row0[j] + row1[j+1]; long rhs = row0[j+1] + row1[j]; if (lhs > rhs) return false;`. row1 for iteration i becomes row0 for i+1, so you can carry the pointer and avoid one multiply per outer step.
perf.rationale: Eliminates the i*n / (i+1)*n multiplies from the inner loop, reducing address-generation work and shortening the index dependency chain; pointer-walking is friendlier to Burst's addressing and SIMD recognition.
perf.risk: None; identical loads and comparison. Use long for the base offset to avoid int overflow if m*n exceeds int range (matches the existing implicit widening).

perf.summary: Same row-base recomputation as CheckMonge: i*n and (i+1)*n folded into four index expressions per inner iteration.
perf.currentCost: Per (i,j): two row-base multiplies and four address computations feeding a 3-operation arithmetic chain plus a sign compare.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist long* row0 = a + (long)i*n; long* row1 = a + (long)(i+1)*n; before the j loop; inner becomes `long d = row0[j] - row1[j] - row0[j+1] + row1[j+1]; if (d < 0) return false;`. Carry row1 into the next outer iteration's row0 to save one multiply per row.
perf.rationale: Removes the per-inner-iteration multiplies and tightens address generation; pure load/arith pattern auto-vectorizes better under Burst.
perf.risk: None; identical arithmetic and branch. Widen base offset to long to preserve indexing semantics for large m*n.
